title: SpaceX Just Got FCC Approval for ONE MILLION Space AI Satellites?!

raw_text: So check this out, because this sounds straight out of sci-fi! The FCC just gave SpaceX conditional approval to build Starmind, a massive constellation of up to one million satellites acting as solar-powered AI data centers in space. We already know terrestrial data centers are choking on power grids and water demands, so moving compute to orbit is a wild idea. Here's the wild part, though: SpaceX has until November 2040 to finish the rollout, and the FCC still hasn't signed off on debris plans above 600 kilometers. Honestly, this is huge if it actually works, because orbital compute could change AI infrastructure forever. At the same time, I'm super skeptical—astrophysicists are pointing out that dissipating heat in a vacuum is like trapping warmth inside a thermos, and upgrading aging AI chips in orbit sounds like a nightmare. Still, watching SpaceX push for a million satellites in space is peak tech drama, and I cannot wait to see how this plays out!

title: Neuralink Gets FDA Greenlight for Pivotal Brain Implant Trial in ALS!
summary: Neuralink received FDA approval to launch LINK, its first U.S. pivotal clinical trial evaluating an implantable brain-computer interface for adults with severe paralysis caused by ALS. The multi-site study will track safety and performance over roughly two years while building on prior PRIME and CAN-PRIME studies involving more than 30 implanted participants.
raw_text: Honestly, this is huge for brain-computer interfaces! Neuralink just announced that the FDA cleared LINK, its very first pivotal clinical trial in the United States for an implantable brain chip aimed at patients with severe paralysis from ALS. So check this out: unlike earlier feasibility studies, a pivotal trial is designed to generate the clinical evidence needed to support an actual commercial marketing application down the road. Over 30 people have already received implants across prior U.S., Canadian, and U.K. studies, and this new trial will follow participants for around two years. Here's the wild part: we're seeing real progress toward giving people with severe motor loss dependable digital control of their devices. I want to stay grounded because it's still investigational and doesn't restore movement or speech on its own, yet watching BCI technology cross into pivotal U.S. trials is genuinely thrilling. We are witnessing medical tech history unfold in real time!

title: 1Password Hacked via Employee GitHub Account—Are Your Passwords Safe?
summary: 1Password disclosed that an attacker accessed internal backend systems after compromising an employee's corporate GitHub account using a stolen token, exposing administrative metadata and certain link tokens for a subset of customers. The company confirmed that encrypted password vaults, Secret Keys, and recovery keys were never accessible.
raw_text: So check this out, because any breach involving a password manager immediately gets our attention! 1Password disclosed a backend intrusion that started when an attacker compromised an employee's corporate GitHub account via a stolen token. Here's the wild part: the intruder accessed CI/CD infrastructure and pushed malicious code to download administrative account records—like names, login emails, and certain link tokens—for a subset of users. Honestly, this is huge as a reminder to lock down developer accounts and tighten phishing defenses. The good news I want to highlight right away is that 1Password says zero-knowledge encryption held strong—your actual vaults, Secret Keys, and master credentials were never accessed. Still, stolen emails and metadata mean targeted phishing is a real risk, so we should all stay extra sharp and enable strong hardware-backed authentication wherever possible.
